interfaces.name: Entropic optimal transport
interfaces.type_shape: Entropic OT with positive regularization, a possibly negative lower-semicontinuous cost, and KL against the product reference measure.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Entropic OT with positive regularization, a possibly negative lower-semicontinuous cost, and KL against the product reference measure.

members.statement_original:
EOT is a convexification of the classical OT problem by means of an entropic penalty. For a regularization parameter $\varepsilon>0$, EOT is given by

\[
\mathsf{OT}_{c,\varepsilon}(\mu,\nu)\coloneqq\inf_{\pi\in\Pi(\mu,\nu)}\int c\,d\pi+\varepsilon\mathsf{D}_{\mathsf{KL}}(\pi\|\mu\otimes\nu),
\]
(4)

evidence.location: Section 2.1 — entropic optimal transport (4) — naming context

interfaces.name: GW distance
interfaces.type_shape: The (2,2)-GW distance is the square root of the optimized squared distortion. The four-fold product integrand uses squared Euclidean distances in possibly different dimensions.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: The (2,2)-GW distance is the square root of the optimized squared distortion. The four-fold product integrand uses squared Euclidean distances in possibly different dimensions.

members.statement_original:
Towards a complete resolution,
one of our main contributions is to quantify the empirical convergence rate of the $(2,2)$-GW distance between Euclidean mm spaces $(\mathbb{R}^{d_{x}},\|\cdot\|,\mu)$ and $(\mathbb{R}^{d_{y}},\|\cdot\|,\nu)$ of different dimensions. Abbreviating $\Delta^{\mathbb{R}^{d_{x}},\mathbb{R}^{d_{y}}}_{2}=\Delta$, the distance of interest is

\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathsf{D}(\mu,\nu) & \coloneqq\inf_{\pi\in\Pi(\mu,\nu)}\|\Delta\|_{L^{2}(\pi\otimes\pi)} \\ =\inf_{\pi\in\Pi(\mu,\nu)}\left(\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_{x}}\times\mathbb{R}^{d_{y}}}\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d_{x}}\times\mathbb{R}^{d_{y}}}\big|\|x-x^{\prime}\|^{2}-\|y-y^{\prime}\|^{2}\big|^{2}d\pi\otimes\pi(x,y,x^{\prime},y^{\prime})\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}.
\end{aligned}
\]
(7)

We drop subscripts from our notation because we focus on the $(2,2)$-GW case from here on out. For finiteness we will always assume $\mu\in\mathcal{P}_{4}(\mathbb{R}^{d_{x}})$ and $\nu\in\mathcal{P}_{4}(\mathbb{R}^{d_{y}})$.

interfaces.name: Entropic regularization
interfaces.type_shape: The entropic functional uses squared L2 distortion and no square root; at zero regularization its source convention is D squared. This is not a debiased Sinkhorn divergence.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: The entropic functional uses squared L2 distortion and no square root; at zero regularization its source convention is D squared. This is not a debiased Sinkhorn divergence.

members.statement_original:
We also treat the GW distance with entropic regularization, which, for $\varepsilon>0$, is defined as

\[
\mathsf{S}_{\varepsilon}(\mu,\nu)\coloneqq\inf_{\pi\in\Pi(\mu,\nu)}\|\Delta\|^{2}_{L^{2}(\pi\otimes\pi)}+\varepsilon\mathsf{D}_{\mathsf{KL}}(\pi\|\mu\otimes\nu).
\]

interfaces.name: EGW functional
interfaces.type_shape: Components S^1 and S_epsilon^2 of the centered decomposition; superscripts are labels, not powers. The second component can be negative. Retain the printed sum indices d1,d2.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Components S^1 and S_epsilon^2 of the centered decomposition; superscripts are labels, not powers. The second component can be negative. Retain the printed sum indices d1,d2.

members.statement_original:
Next, by expanding the $(2,2)$-GW cost, we split the EGW functional into two terms as

\[
\mathsf{S}_{\varepsilon}(\mu,\nu)=\mathsf{S}^{1}(\mu,\nu)+\mathsf{S}^{2}_{\varepsilon}(\mu,\nu),
\]
(8)

where

\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathsf{S}^{1}(\mu,\nu)\coloneqq\int\|x-x^{\prime}\|^{4}d\mu\otimes\mu(x,x^{\prime})+\int\|y-y^{\prime}\|^{4}d\nu\otimes\nu(y,y^{\prime})-4\int\|x\|^{2}\|y\|^{2}d\mu\otimes\nu(x,y) \\ \mathsf{S}^{2}_{\varepsilon}(\mu,\nu)\coloneqq\inf_{\pi\in\Pi(\mu,\nu)}\int-4\|x\|^{2}\|y\|^{2}d\pi(x,y)-8\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}1\leq i\leq d_{1}\\
1\leq j\leq d_{2}\end{subarray}}\Big(\intx_{i}y_{j}d\pi(x,y)\Big)^{2}+\varepsilon\mathsf{D}_{\mathsf{KL}}(\pi\|\mu\otimes\nu).
\end{aligned}
\]

interfaces.name: Cost function
interfaces.type_shape: The theorem binds the explicit quartic/bilinear cost c_A. A ranges over all real dx-by-dy matrices before the attained compact-box restriction.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: The theorem binds the explicit quartic/bilinear cost c_A. A ranges over all real dx-by-dy matrices before the attained compact-box restriction.

members.statement_original: where $\mathsf{OT}_{\mathbf{A},\varepsilon}$ is the EOT problem with cost function $c_{\mathbf{A}}:(x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{x}}\times\mathbb{R}^{d_{y}}\mapsto-4\|x\|^{2}\|y\|^{2}-32x^{\intercal}\mathbf{A}y$.

interfaces.name: Empirical measures
interfaces.type_shape: The source specifies iid samples from each population and empirical measures with equal sample size n; preserve its joint sampling wording.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: The source specifies iid samples from each population and empirical measures with equal sample size n; preserve its joint sampling wording.

members.statement_original: Let $X_{1},\ldots,X_{n}$ and $Y_{1},\ldots,Y_{n}$ be independently and identically distributed (i.i.d.) samples from $\mu$ and $\nu$, respectively, and denote their empirical measures by $\hat{\mu}_{n}=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\delta_{X_{i}}$ and $\hat{\nu}_{n}=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\delta_{Y_{i}}$.

interfaces.name: Sub-Weibull
interfaces.type_shape: Exponential absolute-norm condition with parameter sigma squared in the denominator. Theorem 2 specializes beta to four and uses a common strictly positive parameter. The definition permits sigma=0 without stating a division-by-zero convention.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Exponential absolute-norm condition with parameter sigma squared in the denominator. Theorem 2 specializes beta to four and uses a common strictly positive parameter. The definition permits sigma=0 without stating a division-by-zero convention.

members.statement_original: A probability distribution $\rho\in\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^{d})$ is called $\beta$-sub-Weibull with parameter $\sigma^{2}$ for $\sigma\geq 0$ if $\int\exp\left(\|x\|^{\beta}/2\sigma^{2}\right)d\rho(x)\leq 2$.

interfaces.name: Absolute moment
interfaces.type_shape: Absolute pth moment and the finite-moment probability class, with p in [1,infinity). In Theorem 1 the fourth-moment class and second-moment product have different roles.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Absolute pth moment and the finite-moment probability class, with p in [1,infinity). In Theorem 1 the fourth-moment class and second-moment product have different roles.

members.statement_original: For $p\in[1,\infty)$, let $\mathcal{P}_{p}(\mathbb{R}^{d})$ be the space of Borel probability measures with finite $p$-th absolute moment, i.e., $M_{p}(\rho)\coloneqq\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}}\|x\|^{p}d\rho(x)<\infty$ for any $\rho\in\mathcal{P}_{p}(\mathbb{R}^{d})$.

interfaces.name: KL divergence
interfaces.type_shape: Extended relative entropy: integral when absolutely continuous, plus infinity otherwise; no truncation or symmetrization.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Extended relative entropy: integral when absolutely continuous, plus infinity otherwise; no truncation or symmetrization.

members.statement_original: where the KL divergence is given by $\mathsf{D}_{\mathsf{KL}}(\alpha\|\beta)\coloneqq\int\log(d\alpha/d\beta)\,d\alpha$ if $\alpha\ll\beta$, and equals $+\infty$ otherwise.

interfaces.name: Centered
interfaces.type_shape: Explicit centering convention for the subsequent dual decomposition. Translation invariance permits recentering but does not make raw moments of uncentered measures interchangeable with centered moments.
interfaces.semantic_boundary: Explicit centering convention for the subsequent dual decomposition. Translation invariance permits recentering but does not make raw moments of uncentered measures interchangeable with centered moments.

members.statement_original: Towards the dual form, first observe that $\mathsf S_\varepsilon$ is invariant to isometric operations on the marginal spaces, such as translation and orthonormal rotation. Thus, without loss of generality (w.l.o.g.), we assume that $\mu$ and $\nu$ are centered, i.e., $\int x\,d\mu(x)=\int y\,d\nu(y)=0$.

D3.D1: The infimum is over couplings with the fixed marginals.
D3.D11: The penalty is KL relative to the product of the marginals.

D4.D1: The quadratic distortion is minimized over couplings.
D4.D10: The paper explicitly assumes fourth absolute moments for finiteness.

D5.D1: Optimization is over couplings of the two marginals.
D5.D4: Delta is the quadratic Euclidean distortion specified in (7), with the paper-wide fourth-moment domain.
D5.D11: The entropic penalty is KL relative to the product marginal measure.

D6.D1: The second component optimizes over couplings and their mixed moments.
D6.D11: Its penalty is the source KL divergence.
D6.D5: The left side is the entropic GW functional.
D6.D12: The preceding section convention centers both marginals before this decomposition.

D7.D3: OT_A,epsilon means the EOT problem specialized to the displayed cost.
